source_refs.note: Topic 22.3.1 with the book's insect data (PDF 197-198). The printed chart labels its y-axis 'Abundance (%)' while its scale and steps use counts; the original chart plots counts and adds the percentages as labels.

blocks.text: A bar chart displays categorical data with rectangular bars whose length or height is proportional to the value represented. It compares quantities across distinct categories, such as counts of species, experimental groups or measurements from samples. Categories go on the x-axis, values or frequencies on the y-axis, and bars may be vertical or horizontal.

blocks.caption: Relative abundance of insect species (book's data)

items: Purpose and data: compare the abundance of five insect species; the categorical variable is species and the numerical variable is the number counted.
Axes: species on the x-axis, number of individuals on the y-axis.
Scale: the greatest value is 120 (ants), so scale the y-axis from 0 to 140 in steps of 20.
Bars: draw each bar to its value, with equal widths and even spacing.
Labels and title: title 'Insect species abundance in local forest'; x-axis 'Insect species'; y-axis 'Number of individuals'.

blocks.alt: A vertical bar chart titled Insect species abundance in a local forest. The x-axis lists ladybug, ant, butterfly, bee and dragonfly; the y-axis, number of individuals, runs from 0 to 140 in steps of 20. Bars reach 45 (16%), 120 (41%), 30 (10%), 75 (26%) and 20 (7%).
blocks.caption: Bar chart of the insect counts (original chart drawn from the book's data).
blocks.long_description: The bar chart compares the counts of five insect species found in a month-long study: ants were most numerous (120, 41% of 290 insects), then bees (75, 26%), ladybugs (45, 16%), butterflies (30, 10%) and dragonflies (20, 7%). Insect species, the categorical variable, are on the x-axis and counts, the numerical variable, on the y-axis, scaled from 0 to 140 in steps of 20; the bars have equal widths and spacing.

blocks.title: Legend
blocks.text: A legend is a key on a chart, graph or map that explains the meaning of the symbols, colours, patterns or labels used, for example which colour stands for which category in a bar chart.

blocks.prompt: The ant count is 120 out of 290 insects. Check its percentage.
blocks.explanation: 120 / 290 x 100 = 41.4, about 41%, as in the table.

items: Bar chart: categories on x, values on y, equal bars.
Scale to just above the largest value; add title, axis labels and a legend if needed.
